category_description: Tax-free savings allowances, ISAs and NS&I products, with the limits and rates that apply this tax year.
subject_meta_title: ISA Allowance 2026/27: How Much You Can Save Tax-Free
subject_meta_description: The £20,000 ISA allowance for 2026/27, how it's shared across ISA types, and the £12,000 cash ISA limit for under-65s from April 2027.
label: Annual ISA allowance
context: The total you can pay into all your ISAs each tax year. From 6 April 2027, under-65s will be able to put no more than £12,000 of it into cash ISAs; the full £20,000 stays available for stocks and shares ISAs.

subject_meta_description: The Junior ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £9,000 per child, separate from the adult ISA allowance, with money locked in until the child turns 18.
label: Junior ISA annual allowance
context: The most that can be paid into a child's Junior ISA each tax year. It doesn't count towards the parent's own ISA allowance.

subject_intro: The Lifetime ISA adds a 25% government bonus to savings for a first home or later life. These are the limits, the age rules and the penalty for other withdrawals.
subject_meta_title: Lifetime ISA 2026/27: Limits, Bonus and Rules
subject_meta_description: Lifetime ISA rules for 2026/27: save up to £4,000 a year for a 25% bonus of up to £1,000, for a first home up to £450,000 or from age 60.
label: Annual Lifetime ISA limit
context: Counts towards the overall £20,000 ISA allowance.

label: Government bonus
context: Added to the money you pay in, not to interest or investment growth.

label: Must open before age
context: You must be 18 or over and under 40 to open a Lifetime ISA.

label: Payments and bonus stop at age
context: The account stays open after 50 and keeps earning interest or investment returns.

label: First-home price limit
context: The home must cost this or less, be bought with a mortgage, and be bought at least 12 months after your first payment in.

label: Charge on other withdrawals
context: Applies to withdrawals for any reason other than a first home, reaching 60, or terminal illness, and can leave you with less than you paid in.
The Lifetime ISA's £4,000 limit sits inside this overall allowance.

label: Personal Savings Allowance: basic rate taxpayers
context: Interest up to this amount each tax year is tax-free.

context: Additional rate taxpayers pay tax on all savings interest outside tax-free accounts.

label: Starting rate for savings (maximum)
context: Extra tax-free interest for people with low other income. Every £1 of other income above the Personal Allowance reduces it by £1.
